channel.title: CNS Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Cell, Nature, and Science.

item.title: Science: Ancient DNA unveils distinctive ancestries in the Bronze and Iron Ages of East Tianshan
Science: Multi-organelle signatures map cell-state diversity and metabolic adaptation in tissues
Science: Atmospheric methane lifetime during the Last Glacial Maximum was reduced owing to dust-mediated chlorine chemistry
Science: Splenic regulation of systemic platelet activation state
Science: An expert-level generalist AI for abdominal CT diagnosis
Science: Germline EGFR T790M mutation and lung cancer risk
Science: Nuclear tests at Mt. Mantap have reactivated intraplate faults
Science: Transcriptome-based classification in mice with ASD-risk mutations
Science: Fast, continuous, and coherent atom reloading in a neutral-atom qubit array
Science: A noncontiguous code for RNA-guided DNA recognition at the origin of CRISPR-Cas
Science: VIPR RNA-guided DNA recognition by noncontiguous geometric triplex formation
Science: Extreme loss suppression in an ultracold molecular gas with widely tunable dipolar interactions
Science: Quantum jumps of sound
Science: Disorder-promoted stability
Science: Protecting tropical forests is more cost-effective for biodiversity and climate than restoration
Cell: Phosphate backbone epitranscriptomics: Discovery of natural RNA phosphorothioates and their writer machinery
item.description: Phosphorothioates, stereospecific modifications of the RNA phosphate backbone in anaerobic archaea, expand the epitranscriptome beyond nucleobases and ribose sugars. Installed by Esti enzymes at conserved rRNA and tRNA hotspots, these environmentally responsive marks stabilize tRNAs and support growth at high temperatures.

item.title: Cell: 3D chromatin remodeling during domestication defines novel targets for crop improvement
item.description: Population-level 3D genome atlas of 34 semi-wild and 267 cultivated allotetraploid cottons reveals domestication-selected chromatin conformations that enhance cotton fiber quality and unlock cryptic breeding targets.

item.title: Nature: Mechanisms of Transcriptional Regulation by Salicylic Acid Receptors
Nature: Evolution and heterogeneity of lethal metastatic bladder cancer subtypes
item.description: A rapid autopsy programme provides valuable resources to enable detailed molecular and genetic analyses of the temporal evolution of aggressive histological subtypes and therapy resistance in metastatic bladder cancer.

item.title: Nature: Molecular-level observation of the self-assembly of a virus-like particle
item.description: Using mass photometry combined with a single-molecule trapping method allows real-time monitoring of the assembly of individual virus-like particles with molecular resolution, enabling observation and quantification of their self-assembly pathways and dynamics.

item.title: Nature: Sex without crossovers mimics clonal reproduction in Rhynchospora tenuis
item.description: Rhynchospora tenuis undergoes obligate, genome-wide achiasmy in both male and female meiosis.

item.title: Nature: Identification of broadly tumour-reactive γδ TCRs from multiple myeloma
item.description: A machine-learning algorithm, PreGame, is developed to identify tumour-reactive γδ T cells from single-cell CITE sequencing data, and expansion of this cell population can be used as a biomarker of therapeutic response.

item.title: Nature: Developmental xenocortication using human-derived organoids in mice
item.description: Xenocortication with human neurons enables circuit- and behaviour-level analysis of neurodevelopment in mice.

item.title: Nature: Mutational constraints on RSV F and its neutralization by antibodies
item.description: How respiratory syncytial virus mutations affect antibody neutralization is defined, and a biophysical model of the mechanism is provided, to show how Fab potency and epitope specificity combine to determine the effects of viral mutations on antibody neutralization.

item.title: Nature: A retinoic acid autoregulatory loop governing prefrontal–motor arealization
item.description: MEIS2 , encoding a transcription factor linked to intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, is a key hub of a retinoic-acid-associated gene regulatory network.

item.title: Nature: Scalable near-real-time Bayesian phylogenetics for outbreaks with Delphy
item.description: Delphy makes near-real-time and scalable Bayesian phylogenetics possible for growing viral outbreaks, enabling public health bodies anywhere to analyse and react to their own data with state-of-the-art accuracy and minimal friction.

item.title: Nature: Development of a random background to understand ligand optimization
item.description: An approach to improve efficiency and establish a background expectation for ligand potency optimization is described.

item.title: Nature: Mitochondrial fission factor senses and governs ferroptosis
item.description: The mitochondrial–peroxisomal fission adaptor MFF is identified as a selective pro-ferroptotic mediator, and the newly developed MFF–SPARK sensor enables high-content screening of ferroptosis-sensitizing compounds and the discovery of upstream regulators of MFF.

item.title: Nature: Topographic structure and function of locus coeruleus noradrenaline neurons
item.description: Dorsal and ventral noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus form topographic subpopulations whose projection patterns and activity encode choice switching, reward-prediction errors and disregard of reward-predictive cues, supporting flexible learning behaviour.

item.title: Nature: Transcriptional activation of plant immunity by salicylic acid
item.description: A mechanistic basis for how the hormone salicylic acid promotes transcriptional activation during plant immune responses is described.

item.title: Nature: Targeted genomic integration and rearrangement using prime assembly
item.description: Prime assembly enables RNA-guided integration of medium-to-large DNA sequences in human cells without requiring double-strand breaks or cell cycle progression, and supports exon recoding, transgene insertion and megabase-scale rearrangements.

item.title: Nature: Cohesin reshapes replication fork contacts to aid fork slowing and reversal
item.description: Cohesin-mediated loop extrusion limits sister-fork coupling and tethers nearby replication forks under replication stress, promoting fork reversal and slowing fork progression to safeguard genome stability.

item.title: Nature: Reimagining research papers as interactive and reliable AI agents
item.description: Paper2Agent converts research papers into interactive artificial intelligence agents by turning manuscripts, code and data into model context protocol-based tool-invoking systems that reproduce original results, answer new scientific queries and collaborate to generate novel insights.

item.title: Nature: Rapid patient-specific neural networks for X-ray to volume registration
item.description: xvr makes pan-anatomical 2D/3D rigid registration accessible to broad clinical and research communities.

item.title: Cell: Gliomas phenocopy an inborn error of metabolism to drive neuronal activity and tumor growth
item.description: Glioma-derived guanidinoacetate depolarizes neighboring neurons through γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) A receptors, and depleting this metabolite reduces both neuronal activity and glioma growth.

item.title: Cell: Single-cell-resolved genome atlas of prokaryoplankton inhabiting the ocean’s interior
item.description: GORG-Dark presents genomes of 9,698 individual bacterial and archaeal cells from the ocean’s sunless interior. The atlas resolves depth stratification to abyssal waters, uncovers particle-attached Pelagibacterales, maps chemolithoautotrophy and biosynthetic gene clusters, and identifies a rhodopsin clade specific to the dark ocean.

item.title: Cell: Programmed ribosomal frameshifting triggers translational stress to promote viral replication
item.description: Viruses such as SARS-CoV-2 can use programmed ribosomal frameshifting to turn off host translation and promote viral replication, expanding the known uses of programmed ribosomal frameshifting by viruses.

item.title: Nature: Quality control of glycogen through direct ubiquitylation by RNF213
Cell: Norway spruce spatiotemporal programs of conifer reproductive development
item.description: Spatiotemporal transcriptomics across conifer reproductive and vegetative shoots reveals candidate developmental regulators and evolutionarily conserved tissue patterning genes in seed plants.

item.title: Cell: Copper ion-induced MYH9 polymerization executes cuproptosis
item.description: Copper binding drives MYH9 polymerization, triggering cytoskeletal collapse and cuproptosis. HThPA releases intracellular copper through glutathione depletion, exposing a therapeutic vulnerability in drug-resistant tumors.

item.title: Nature: Encoded and non-genetic protein variants expand human functional proteome
Cell: Metax enables accurate cross-domain taxonomic profiling of metagenomes
item.description: Metax is a cross-domain metagenomic profiler that uses genome-wide coverage evidence to improve species-level microbial profiling and distinguish supported taxa from artifacts. Across diverse datasets, Metax enables robust taxonomic profiling, pathogen detection, contamination assessment, and discovery of disease-associated bacterial and viral signatures.

item.title: Cell: Mitochondrial ATP promotes T cell differentiation through chromatin accessibility
item.description: Cell-mediated immunity requires cytotoxic CD8+ T cells that adopt and maintain an effector phenotype. Here, D-α-hydroxybutyrate (DAHB) is shown to act as a metabolic adjuvant, driving the conversion of proliferating CD8+ T cells into cytotoxic effector cells by linking mitochondrial ATP production to chromatin remodeling and gene expression.

item.title: Cell: Glycocalyx-edited mesenchymal stem/stromal cell therapy in advanced osteoporosis
item.description: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-based therapy holds promise for reversal of bone loss in osteoporosis. This phase 1 study establishes the safety and feasibility of intravenous administration of glycocalyx-engineered human MSCs and provides evidence that MSCs derived from the bone marrow of older individuals with osteoporosis retain clinically meaningful osteoregenerative capacity.

item.title: Cell: Architecture of the serotonergic projectome in the mouse brain
item.description: Serotonin neurons innervate nearly the entire mammalian brain, yet how their projections are organized has remained unclear. Systematic whole-brain serotonergic axon collateralization mapping reveals five projectomic groups that preferentially target functionally related regions, with each projectomic group connecting to specific spatial transcriptomic and behavioral profiles.

item.title: Cell: Caloric restriction modulates genome-wide somatic mutation in mice
item.description: Mutations accumulate in cells with age, while caloric restriction extends lifespan across diverse animals. Grońska-Pęski et al. study the effect of caloric restriction on mutations genome-wide in mice, finding reduced mutation burdens across several tissues and cell types, thereby establishing that diet can alter mutation accumulation genome-wide during aging.

item.title: Nature: Highly efficient base editing at PCSK9 and normal human embryo development
Nature: Predicting genome-wide functional constraints with GPN-Star
item.description: GPN-Star, a genomic language model with a phylogeny-aware architecture for whole-genome alignment data, is shown to be a scalable and flexible tool for genetic variant effect prediction across species.

item.title: Nature: Imaging cellular activity across all organs reveals body-wide circuits
item.description: An imaging system developed to record cellular activity throughout the whole body of zebrafish captures cellular organ dynamics and identifies multiple distributed circuits.

item.title: Nature: TRI-611, a selective, brain-penetrant molecular glue degrader of ALK
item.description: TRI-611 induces the degradation of ALK fusion proteins via a previously undescribed CRBN recruitment motif, and its preclinical anti-tumour activity highlights TRI-611 as a potential new way of treating ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer.

item.title: Nature: TM184C is a GPCR-like regulator of intercellular exchange and autophagy
item.description: TM184C—an ancient G-protein-coupled receptor-like superdark protein involved in regulation of autophagy, intercellular connectivity and material exchange—underscores the promise of exploring the understudied human proteome and beyond.

item.title: Nature: Within-family effect of ancestry on complex traits in a Mexican population
item.description: This study uses a within-family design to identify significant ancestry differences in complex traits such as height and type 2 diabetes in a genetically diverse population from Mexico City.

item.title: Nature: Denisovans from southwestern China and their subsistence strategies
item.description: Evidence from Bianfu Cave shows specialized hunting, expedient stone-tool production and extensive bone use of Denisovans, providing new insights into their ecology, behaviour and cultural legacy in eastern Asia.

item.title: Nature: A serpin–myeloid axis in pancreatic cancer heterogeneity and immune evasion
item.description: SERPINE1 and SERPINB2-driven fibrin-rich niches locally programme immunosuppressive macrophages and exclude T cells, enabling spatially organized immune evasion in pancreatic ductal carcinoma.

item.title: Nature: Ancient proteins identify various Denisovan remains from Southwest China
item.description: Identification and proteomic analysis of bone fragments and teeth from an excavation in Southwest China provide insight into the evolution and phenotype of Denisovans and fill a geographical gap in their documented distribution.

item.title: Nature: Proximity-guided graph learning reveals tumour-associated proximity antigens
item.description: A proximity-mapping atlas defines tumour-associated proximity antigens, revealing disease-associated membrane spatial communities, and identifies EGFR–CDCP1 as a co-target pair that enhances tumour killing by multispecific therapeutics.

item.title: Nature: Breaking timescales with generative sampling of conformational transitions
item.description: A generative committor-guided path-sampling framework reconstructs rare biomolecular transition pathways and reveals the underlying thermodynamics and kinetics without using predefined collective variables or brute-force sampling, at an acceptable computational cost.

item.title: Nature: Neocortical long-range inhibition promotes cortical synchrony and sleep
item.description: In mice, a sparse population of sleep-active long-range inhibitory neurons in the neocortex promote widespread cortical synchronization and sleep, revealing a cortical mechanism that contributes to the regulation of sleep.

item.title: Nature: An operational perturbation proteomics-based virtual cell model
item.description: Temporal protein-abundance measurements from systematically perturbed breast cancer cell lines were generated to develop ProteinTalks, a virtual cell model that functions as an operational tool for diverse drug discovery tasks.

item.title: Nature: PLA2G2D in tumour-draining lymph nodes regulates anti-tumour immunity
item.description: A specific population of macrophages that express high levels of the enzyme PLA2G2D in tumour-draining lymph nodes is associated with poor prognosis in patients, and inhibiting PLA2G2D improves anti-tumour immunity in mouse models.

item.title: Nature: Integrated signatures define mutational processes in prostate cancer
item.description: Eight integrated mutational footprints collectively explain the mutational processes in 85% of primary prostate cancer genomes.

item.title: Cell: Structural basis of a SWI/SNF-associated transcription pre-initiation complex
item.description: Cryo-EM and genetic analyses reveal that the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeler is an integral component of the transcription pre-initiation complex. The structures demonstrate how SWI/SNF facilitates transcription initiation through stabilization of PIC organization and concerted remodeling of the +1 nucleosome.

item.title: Cell: Identification of the tendon/ligament stem cell in mice and humans
item.description: The tendon/ligament stem cell is identified, and dysregulation of differentiation in this cell is shown as a mechanism contributing to lumbar spinal stenosis.

item.title: Cell: Tabula Sapiens 2.0: A comprehensive transcriptomic atlas of human cell types
item.description: An expanded atlas of human cells maps the expression of nearly all human transcription factors across 701 cell-type/tissue combinations and uncovers the heterogeneous nature of senescence across tissues and cell types.

item.title: Nature: Rewiring the ribosome to translate proteins encoded in its own RNA
item.description: Bacterial ribosomes can synthesize proteins encoded within their own RNA.

item.title: Nature: Connectome analysis of a cerebellum-like circuit for sensory prediction
item.description: Connectomics, electrophysiology and modelling of electric fish neural circuits shows how distributed synaptic plasticity across multiple network layers cooperates to enable fast, accurate and noise-robust sensory learning.

item.title: Nature: Intracellular complement factor H protects neurons during CNS inflammation
item.description: CFH is a key mediator of neuronal resilience across the central nervous system in mice and humans.

item.title: Nature: Late-life semaglutide treatment slows ageing and extends lifespan in female mice
item.description: Semaglutide treatment for 3 months in female mice improved physiological function, attenuated hallmarks of ageing and modulated nutrient sensors and conserved genetic regulators of ageing.

item.title: Nature: The nutritional value of invertebrate aquatic foods
item.description: Aquatic invertebrates are exceptionally nutrient dense, supplying the equivalent annual vitamin B 12 and selenium requirements for over 5 billion people.

item.title: Cell: Oxygen-responsive bacterial glycosphingolipid links symbiont fitness and immune development in neonatal host
item.description: How do maternal gut bacteria seed the rapidly developing neonatal gut? Heo et al. show that Bacteroides fragilis produces a distinct membrane lipid that enables this strict anaerobe to tolerate a microaerobic environment. This finding highlights divergent evolutionary strategies among related species, most of which rely on lipids conferring broader fitness.

item.title: Cell: Ratiometric transcriptional activation by protein degradation
item.description: By tethering a protein of interest to anti-CRISPR, protein degradation is transformed into amplified and programmable transcriptional outputs via Cas-based transcription factors, with sensitivity to protein loss tuned by the anti-CRISPR-Cas ratio. These synthetic circuits can be multiplexed to enable high-throughput discovery of protein-degrading and -destabilizing molecules.

item.title: Cell: De novo pan-rhodamine binders for fluorescence microscopy from mammalian cells to extremophiles
item.description: We developed an AI-based and principled computational strategy for de novo design of Rhobins, compact pan-rhodamine binders with high brightness, reversible binding, and extreme stability. It enables superior live-/fixed-cell, super-resolution, and single-molecule imaging with properties surpassing existing tags. It also supports extremophile imaging at 75°C, inaccessible with current tools.

item.title: Cell: Cross-species single-cell atlas of the striatum defines cell-type and subregion disease vulnerabilities
item.description: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial validation across human and mouse striatum define principles of neuronal specialization across cell types, subregions, and species. These findings lay the foundation for understanding cell- and subregion-resolved contributions to brain function and disease, including addiction risk, antipsychotic responses, Huntington’s disease vulnerabilities, and pharmacologically relevant species differences.

item.title: Cell: Live-cell transcriptomics with engineered virus-like particles
item.description: Najia, Le, Borrajo et al. establish “cellular self-reporting,” a technology to export molecular analytes from cells in virus-like particles. The authors demonstrate how mRNA export enables longitudinal transcriptome-wide profiling of living cells by sampling cell media. This platform transcends the destructive nature of conventional transcriptomic analysis methods and reveals gene expression dynamics in complex biological systems in situ.

item.title: Cell: Endogenous opioid dynamics in the dorsal striatum sculpt neural activity to promote goal-directed action
item.description: Cell-type-specific, time-locked release of the opioid neuropeptide dynorphin in the dorsomedial striatum is both necessary and sufficient for goal-directed behavior. Inputs from the basolateral amygdala trigger dynorphin release that engages retrograde Gi-coupled presynaptic inhibition via the kappa opioid receptor, revealing a rapid neuropeptide mechanism for shaping behavior.

item.title: Cell: Genome-scale perturb-seq in primary human CD4+ T cells maps context-specific regulators of T cell programs and human immune traits
item.description: A dynamic atlas of gene regulation was generated by perturbing every expressed gene across 22 million primary human CD4+ T cells under resting conditions and following re-stimulation. The resulting map reveals context-specific regulators of immune programs and links regulatory pathways to naturally occurring T cell states and autoimmune disease risk.

item.title: Cell: Human nuclear ribomes reveal DNA-embedded ribonucleotides as epigenetic modulators of transcription-associated DNA supercoiling
item.description: Human nuclear ribomes reveal that DNA-embedded ribonucleotides accumulate at promoter-associated regulatory elements and scale with transcriptional activity. RNase H2 and Top1 process these ribonucleotides to modulate DNA supercoiling, uncovering a previously unrecognized epigenetic mechanism underlying transcription.

item.title: Nature: A binding-to-release strategy for targeted anticancer drug delivery
item.description: A binding-to-release drug conjugate strategy enables targeted payload release without cellular internalization, improving tumour specificity, efficacy and expanding therapeutic targets beyond conventional drug conjugates.

item.title: Cell: Integrative spatial profiling of 3D genome organization and gene expression in tissue
item.description: Spatial Hi-C-RNA simultaneously maps genome architecture and gene expression from the same tissue, revealing how spatial genome organization shapes cellular identity, development, and tumor evolution beyond what transcriptomics alone can capture.

item.title: Cell: DDIAS shields single-stranded DNA in mitosis and promotes vertebrate brain development
item.description: DDIAS is identified as a factor that protects single-stranded DNA during mitosis to maintain chromosome stability, and inactivating mutations in DDIAS are identified in a human neurodevelopmental disorder.

item.title: Cell: Gut microbiota generate dinitrosyl iron complexes with cardiometabolic benefits
item.description: Gut bacteria convert inorganic nitrate and non-heme iron into bioactive dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) that distribute systemically and signal independently of free nitric oxide. These microbe-derived DNICs protect against cardiometabolic disease and fatty liver by restoring compromised metabolic signaling pathways.

item.title: Cell: RNA structures regulate norovirus life cycle and enable rational attenuation in vivo
item.description: Genome-wide mapping of RNA structure in murine norovirus reveals structural elements whose disruption impairs viral replication in cells and in vivo. Such structural disruptions generate a genetically stable virus that elicits protective immunity in vivo, offering a rational strategy for RNA virus vaccine design.

item.title: Nature: Family genetic designs in MoBa provide insights into health and functioning
item.description: The Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study demonstrates how family-based genomic data can disentangle direct genetic effects from confounding, improving studies of health and human development.

item.title: Nature: An Icelandic pangenome reference
item.description: Newly developed methods enable construction of Icelandic haplotypes and mapping of population-scale short reads to a pangenome by reducing reference bias and improving discovery in low-mappability regions, revealing many novel variants, including pathogenic alleles.

item.title: Cell: Mutually beneficial interactions between bacteria and Arabidopsis promote phosphorus nutrition and growth
item.description: Over 20% of root-associated bacteria promote Arabidopsis seedling growth under phosphorus (P) deficiency in a host-dependent manner. Further analyses showed that P-deficient plants secrete malate to attract Acinetobacter species to the rhizoplane, where the bacteria utilize plant-secreted nitrogen and carbon sources to fuel P mobilization that benefits both parties.

item.title: Cell: Multimodal brain cell atlas across the adult macaque lifespan
item.description: A multimodal single-nucleus atlas of 2,955,873 nuclei spanning eight macaque brain regions across the adult lifespan, including exceptionally old individuals, reveals region-specific and shared patterns of cellular vulnerability during aging. This framework provides a basis for dissecting shared and divergent molecular programs underlying primate brain aging, longevity, and neurodegeneration.

item.title: Cell: Ancient genomes reveal distinct human dispersals and social stratification in the settlement history of western Remote Oceania
item.description: The peopling of Remote Oceania involved some of humanity’s greatest expansions into the open ocean. Ancient DNA spanning the last 3,000 years from the Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Fiji, and Tonga reveals the sources and timing of dispersals following the initial settlement and uncovers social practices of an early Fijian community that experienced recent Papuan-related gene flow.

item.title: Cell: Brain perivascular macrophages regulate endothelial cell function via a cMAF-dependent transcriptional program in mouse and human
item.description: This study identifies cMAF as a key transcription factor that orchestrates the molecular crosstalk between brain perivascular macrophages and arteries, thereby sustaining cerebrovascular function in health and disease.

item.title: Cell: Functional atlas of vertebrate viral RNA elements that stabilize RNA and enhance translation
item.description: Functional profiling of ∼200,000 genomic segments from vertebrate-infecting viruses uncovers RNA elements that boost gene expression by stabilizing mRNAs and enhancing translation, revealing the diversity of TENT4-dependent mixed tailing and identifying canonical poly(A) polymerase-mediated cytoplasmic polyadenylation, together expanding our understanding of post-transcriptional regulation and RNA therapeutic design.

item.title: Nature: Biomarkers of nivolumab benefit in resectable non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: Potential predictive biomarkers of perioperative nivolumab therapy benefit in non-small cell lung cancer are identified from evaluable participants in the CheckMate 77T trial.

item.title: Nature: Glucose-responsive probiotics for glycaemic modulation in mice and monkeys
item.description: Engineered probiotics equipped with a synthetic glucose-responsive circuit transiently colonize the gut and secrete therapeutic factors when glucose levels increase, enabling safe, oral, sense-and-respond control of diabetes in mouse and primate models.

item.title: Cell: Convergent evolution of metabolic regulation governs redox adaptation in Toxoplasma
item.description: A protein called TgPRO enables the metabolic adaptation and survival of apicomplexan parasites such as Toxoplasma under oxidative and nutrient stress.

item.title: Cell: The structural basis for LRRK2’s activation and autoinhibition
item.description: Elevated kinase activity in leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is linked to Parkinson’s disease; this study shows that its ROC GTPase acts as a nucleotide-dependent molecular switch that regulates activation and autoinhibition and reveals how some but not all PD mutations disrupt this regulatory switch.

item.title: Nature: Amygdala astrocyte primary cilium mechanisms contribute to stress behaviours
item.description: Amygdala astrocyte primary cilia are disrupted during stress, and their restoration leads to improvements in stress-related behaviour in mice.

item.title: Nature: Antigen presentation by CD40 + MHC-II + astrocytes promotes CNS autoimmunity
item.description: Astrocytes promote central nervous system (CNS) immunity through antigen presentation and activation of CD40 in astrocytes by CD40L expressed by CD4 + T cells in a model of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.

item.title: Nature: The Virtual Tissues foundation model resolves spatial proteomics across scales
item.description: Virtual Tissues (VirTues), a foundation model for spatial proteomics that captures tissue organization across scales, supports marker reconstruction, cell segmentation and typing, niche annotation, spatial biomarker discovery and patient stratification across heterogeneous panels and datasets.

item.title: Nature: Virus reactivation in acute and long COVID-19
item.description: Chronic reactivation of distinct herpesviruses and anelloviruses occur during acute and long COVID-19, and track with disease severity, inflammation and outcomes, revealing immune signatures with prognostic potential.

item.title: Nature: FNIP1 variants are associated with favourable metabolism in 1 million humans
item.description: The FNIP1 pathway has a role in human energy metabolism, and its inhibition is a potential therapeutic strategy in cardiometabolic disease.

item.title: Cell: Metabolic atlas of early human cortex reveals glycolytic remodeling and pentose phosphate pathway control of cell fate transitions
item.description: The developing human cortex is composed of diverse cell types, but how nutrient metabolism shapes their fate has remained unclear. This study maps the metabolic landscape of the developing human cortex and identifies glycolysis and pentose phosphate pathway activity as key regulators of radial glia fate, controlling the generation of outer radial glia and inhibitory neurons.

item.title: Cell: Ultrarapid deep 3D histology enables intraoperative mapping of glioma infiltration
item.description: ULTRA compresses 3D histology from days or hours to within 30 minutes by leveraging the chemical specificity of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy through the synergistic development of rapid tissue clearing and unsupervised AI. The platform enables intraoperative visualization of glioma architecture and depth-dependent tumor infiltration margins.

item.title: Cell: Milk osteopontin alters the infant microbiome to drive DC hematopoiesis and disease tolerance
item.description: Milk-derived osteopontin confers protection from viral or bacterial severe lower respiratory illness by altering the neonatal gut microbiome.

item.title: Cell: Co-option of retrotransposons promotes antibody diversification
item.description: A longstanding mystery in antibody diversification is how AID specifically targets immunoglobulin V genes. Ancient LINE-1 retrotransposons embedded within the immunoglobulin locus provide a recruitment platform for the HUSH complex and AID to drive somatic hypermutation.

item.title: Cell: CRISPR screens identify targets to rescue age-related T cell dysfunction in cancer
item.description: Dusp5 and Zfp219 serve as critical regulators of age-related T cell dysfunction, with the loss of either driving T cells into an effector-like state that improves tumor control through distinct mechanisms within the aged tumor microenvironment.

item.title: Cell: Gasdermin E couples viral pyroptosis to lethal hepatic lipid accumulation
item.description: Wetland virus activates dual apoptotic cascades to trigger GSDME-dependent hepatocyte pyroptosis, which rewires cellular lipid metabolism and ultimately causes severe hepatic steatosis. Therapeutic targeting of this pyroptosis-metabolism axis alleviates lethal wetland virus infection in mice.

item.title: Cell: An Oryza orphan gene confers trans-species drought tolerance
item.description: ROAD1 is an Oryza-specific orphan gene that co-opts conserved ABA signaling to enhance drought tolerance without obvious growth defects or yield penalty under normal conditions. Elite rice lines carrying its functional allele exhibited higher grain yield than controls under drought, and its heterologous expression enhanced drought tolerance across diverse angiosperms.

item.title: Cell: Trichoderma swollenin activates AtABCB5-dependent auxin efflux to promote plant development
item.description: The beneficial fungus Trichoderma acts through the secreted swollenin ThSWO, which crosses the plant cell wall and engages AtABCB5, an auxin efflux carrier, at the host cell surface. This effector-transporter module tunes auxin-associated cellular responses, revealing how beneficial fungi co-opt host hormone transport to promote root development.

item.title: Cell: Condensates of the chromatin regulator ANKRD11 restrict hypertranscribed genes to safeguard development
item.description: ANKRD11 restricts hypertranscribed genes by forming biomolecular condensates that spatially sequester elongation factors, with disruption of this condensate-mediated control leading to aberrant organogenesis and underlying the pathogenesis of developmental disorders like KBG syndrome.

item.title: Cell: Robust regulatory interplay of enhancers, facilitators, and promoters in a native chromatin context
item.description: Using an in situ genome-rewriting platform, Zhou et al. demonstrate that precise transcriptional regulation of the NMU promoter is governed by a 3D regulatory hub comprising a core retroviral LTR enhancer, a decoy LTR promoter, and activity-boosting “facilitator” elements.
